reasoning: The claim distorts the findings of a widely cited March 2023 report by Goldman Sachs economists (Jan Hatzius et al., "The Potentially Large Effects of Artificial Intelligence on Economic Growth"). The report estimated that generative AI could expose the equivalent of up to 300 million full-time jobs globally to automation, not that 300 million jobs will be eliminated or replaced. The authors explicitly emphasized that most jobs and industries are only partially exposed to automation and are far more likely to be complemented by AI rather than substituted outright, alongside anticipated job creation and significant increases in global GDP. Stating definitively that generative AI "will replace 300 million jobs" conflates task automation exposure with total job displacement.
